channel.title: CNS Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from Cell, Nature, and Science.

item.title: Nature: This compound enhances long-term memory of mice — but only in females
item.description: Nature, Published online: 26 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00603-y Acetate helps the female rodents form memories but is less effective in males.

item.title: Nature: Why an industry career move is a taboo topic in academia
item.description: Nature, Published online: 26 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00158-y Adam Levy investigates why researchers are sometimes reluctant to disclose their plans to colleagues.

item.title: Nature: Ultra-sensitive CAR T cells eliminate hard-to-treat tumours in mice
item.description: Nature, Published online: 26 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00622-9 A proof-of-concept study opens up an avenue for treating solid tumours that express low levels of a target antigen.

item.title: Nature: UN creates new scientific AI advisory panel: what will it do?
item.description: Nature, Published online: 26 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00542-8 The panel has been compared to the IPCC – the international panel whose research helped to shape landmark climate agreements.

item.title: Nature: Health effects linger 20 generations after rats are exposed to fungicide
item.description: Nature, Published online: 26 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00555-3 Scientists say the findings are a warning about the kinds of chemical that people are exposed to in the environment.

item.title: Nature: Neanderthal dad, human mum: study reveals ancient procreation pattern
item.description: Nature, Published online: 26 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00583-z Genomic analysis shows that interbreeding between female Neanderthals and human males was less common than the opposite combination.

item.title: Nature: World-first stem-cell therapy shows promise for treating spina bifida in the womb
item.description: Nature, Published online: 26 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00602-z Six pregnant women participated in a small trial in which placenta-derived stem cells were applied to fetal spinal cords and the treatment was found to be safe.

Cell: Large-scale proteomics across neurological disorders uncovers biomarker panel and targets in multiple sclerosis
item.description: Deep proteome profiling of over 5,000 cerebrospinal fluid samples by mass spectrometry maps protein alterations across major neurological disorders, resolving key sources of variation as well as shared and disease-specific signatures. This framework yields a 22-protein assay that improves the differential diagnosis of multiple sclerosis from other inflammatory conditions, particularly in diagnostically challenging oligoclonal band-negative individuals.

item.title: Cell: Vitamin B2 and B3 nutrigenomics reveals a therapy for NAXD disease
item.description: A nutrigenomics framework identifies genetic diseases amenable to vitamin B2 and B3 therapies. This approach nominates vitamin B3 as a therapy for NAXD deficiency, a lethal neurodevelopmental disorder. In this Naxd KO mouse model, vitamin B3 rescues NAD(P)(H) metabolism, prevents brain pathology, and extends lifespan by more than 40-fold.

item.title: Cell: Whole-organ and whole-body 3D atlases enable cellome-wide profiling
item.description: Whole-organ and whole-body atlases at single-cell resolution enable quantitative cellome-wide analysis across development, physiology, and pathology.

item.title: Cell: The MicrobeAtlas database: Global trends and insights into Earth’s microbial ecosystems
item.description: MicrobeAtlas ( www.microbeatlas.org ) is an integrated, reference-based resource for truly planet-wide microbiomics, analyzing hundreds of thousands of microbial lineages across diverse environments, conditions, and technologies.

item.title: Cell: Nuclear speckles enable processing of RNA from GC-rich isochores
item.description: Nuclear speckles are key subnuclear structures that regulate gene expression in GC-rich regions. This work shows that the evolution and expansion of core speckle proteins were crucial for the increased GC content seen in amniote genomes.

item.title: Nature: The surprising science of squeaky sneakers
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00620-x The mystery of why soft shoes squeak on hard floors may be solved, according to new research

item.title: Nature: How an exercise-activated enzyme helps to keep the brain young
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00515-x A protein reinforces the blood–brain barrier, which becomes leaky with age.

item.title: Nature: How earthquakes and lightning help explain squeaky sneakers
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00619-4 High-speed footage reveals shoe squeaks can start with a tiny bolt of lightning — plus, evidence that a debated brain phenomenon exists in humans.

item.title: Nature: Limitations of probing field-induced response with STM
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10126-1 Limitations of probing field-induced response with STM

item.title: Nature: Cavity-altered superconductivity
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-025-10062-6 A new platform making use of hexagonal boron nitride interfaced with the molecular superconductor κ-(BEDT-TTF)2Cu[N(CN)2]Br is demonstrated for realizing cavity-altered materials, confirmed by magnetic force microscopy and nano-optical measurements.

item.title: Nature: Compact deep neural network models of the visual cortex
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10150-1 Parsimonious deep neural network models can be used for prediction of visual neuron responses.

item.title: Nature: Echinoderm stereom gradient structures enable mechanoelectrical perception
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10164-9 Sea urchin spines show exceptional mechanoelectrical sensing from gradient structures and can be replicated in 3D-printed mimics for underwater sensing.

item.title: Nature: A membrane-bound nuclease directly cleaves phage DNA during genome injection
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10207-1 A widespread bacterial defence system called SNIPE is shown to localize to the cell membrane, where it identifies and cleaves the DNA of infecting phage as it is injected into the bacterial cell.

item.title: Nature: Vectorized instructive signals in cortical dendrites
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10190-7 Mice learning a neurofeedback brain–computer interface task show neuron-specific teaching signals in cortical dendrites, consistent with a vectorized solution for credit assignment in the brain.

item.title: Nature: Peripheral immune-inducer dendritic cells drive early-life allergic inflammation
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10162-x Early-life exposure to allergens triggers a distinct local mode of dendritic cell activation in neonatal skin without requiring migration to lymph nodes, which shapes responses to allergens in later life.

item.title: Nature: Pancreatic-targeted lipid nanoparticles based on organ capsule filtration
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10158-7 Elucidation of fundamental pancreatic-targeted mechanisms enables the development of lipid nanoparticles for the precise delivery of nucleic acid therapeutics to the pancreas, highlighting their promising potential in the treatment of pancreatic diseases.

item.title: Nature: Squeaking at soft–rigid frictional interfaces
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10132-3 High-speed imaging reveals that the squeak of soft–rigid frictional interfaces, like sneakers sliding on a basketball court, arises from intersonic opening slip pulses—analogous to earthquake ruptures—that thin ridges on the rubber confine to repeat at a musical frequency.

item.title: Nature: Pivoting colloidal assemblies exhibit mechanical metamaterial behaviour
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10217-z A method is described for the manufacture of pivoting colloidal assemblies comprising rotating diamond and rotating triangle geometries that show tunable folding and unfolding by thermal fluctuations and actuation by magnetic attractions.

item.title: Nature: Clonal-aggregative multicellularity tuned by salinity in a choanoflagellate
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10137-y The choanoflagellate Choanoeca flexa forms motile and contractile cell monolayers purely clonally, purely aggregatively or through a combination of both processes depending on environmental conditions.

item.title: Nature: Convergent MurJ flippase inhibition by phage lysis proteins
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10163-w A common mechanism of inhibition of the essential lipid II flippase MurJ by three distinct phage-encoded single-gene lysis proteins provides insights into potential new targets for antimicrobial development.

item.title: Nature: OR7A10 GPCR engineering boosts CAR-NK therapy against solid tumours
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10149-8 The identification of ‘boosters’ that drive gene overexpression directly in a CAR construct provides a simple and scalable strategy for developing effective CAR-NK cell therapies for solid tumours.

item.title: Nature: A disease model resource reveals core principles of tissue-specific cancer evolution
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10187-2 The Mouse Cancer Cell line Atlas (MCCA) provides major advances towards a mechanistic understanding of cancer genomes.

item.title: Nature: Rewiring an E3 ligase enhances cold resilience and phosphate use in maize
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10142-1 The E3 ubiquitin ligase NLA postively regulates cold tolerance and negatively regulates phosphate uptake in maize, and a genetically engineered variant of this enzyme leads to improved cold tolerance and enhanced phosphate uptake, improving yield in field trials.

item.title: Nature: Field-free full switching of chiral antiferromagnetic order
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10175-6 An Mn3Sn homo-junction enables efficient field-free full switching of chiral antiferromagnets with greatly reduced power consumption, advancing their potential for energy-efficient magnetic memory devices with advantages of ultradense integration and ultrafast speed.

item.title: Nature: Hydrofluorocarbon electrolytes for energy-dense and low-temperature batteries
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10210-6 A method using hydrofluorocarbon electrolytes for synthesizing alkanes with monofluorinated structures is described, yielding a pathway for manufacturing lithium-metal batteries able to achieve high energy density as well as operate at low temperature.

item.title: Nature: Argentine fossil rewrites evolutionary history of a baffling dinosaur clade
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10194-3 A skeleton of the alvarezsauroid Alnashetri cerropoliciensis—representing a highly complete alvarezsauroid skeleton from South America—provides evidence on the evolution of the peculiar anatomy and miniaturization within this unusual theropod dinosaur clade.

item.title: Nature: Coral microbiomes as reservoirs of unknown genomic and biosynthetic diversity
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10159-6 Reconstructing microbial genomes from 820 reef-building corals collected at 99 reefs across 32 islands throughout the Pacific Ocean highlights the importance of conserving coral reefs as vital reservoirs of molecular diversity.

item.title: Nature: CLCC1 promotes hepatic neutral lipid flux and nuclear pore complex assembly
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-025-10064-4 CRISPR–Cas9 screening identifies CLCC1 as a factor that increases neutral lipid flux to prevent hepatic steatosis and promotes nuclear pore complex assembly by promoting membrane bending and fusion.

item.title: Nature: CLCC1 governs ER bilayer equilibration to maintain lipid homeostasis
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10161-y Phospholipid scrambling at the endoplasmic reticulum is essential for establishing a dynamic equilibrium to maintain cellular homeostasis.

item.title: Nature: Functional dissection of complex trait variants at single-nucleotide resolution
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10121-6 Massively parallel reporter assays across five cell types identify thousands of causal, noncoding regulatory variants among 220,000 loci, revealing diverse regulatory mechanisms shaping complex traits and disease.

item.title: Nature: Uncovering origins of heterogeneous superconductivity in La 3 Ni 2 O 7
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-025-10095-x Wide-field quantum sensing shows μm-scale inhomogeneous superconductivity in high-pressure La3Ni2O7, linking local diamagnetic response to stress and stoichiometry and clarifying mechanisms that suppress or enhance superconductivity.

item.title: Nature: Human hippocampal neurogenesis in adulthood, ageing and Alzheimer’s disease
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10169-4 Mapping of neurogenesis in human hippocampi across ages and different cognitive abilities using multiomic single-cell sequencing reveals distinct signatures between cognitive preservation and decline.

item.title: Nature: Entanglement-assisted non-local optical interferometry in a quantum network
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10171-w Entangled quantum memories are used in a quantum network of silicon–vacancy centres in diamond nanocavities to experimentally perform non-local phase measurements.

item.title: Nature: EU leaders should not rush to revamp green-hydrogen rules
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00560-6 Some policymakers think that climate-friendly policies are impeding the adoption of green hydrogen. They should ask scientists to review the evidence.

item.title: Nature: Stem cells provide a potent treatment for frailty
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00584-y Elderly people with frailty, which affects up to one-quarter of over-50s, increased their endurance after a single dose of stem cells.

item.title: Nature: We need a global assessment of avoidable climate-change risks
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00544-6 To understand the urgency of emissions reductions, policymakers and citizens need a full analysis of what is at stake.

item.title: Nature: The age of animal experiments is waning. Where will science go next?
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00563-3 Advances in organ and computer models are raising the prospect that some animal experiments could be eliminated. But there are still huge hurdles to overcome.

item.title: Nature: The protein carriers of hundreds of lipids have been identified
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00570-4 Different types of lipid molecule are transported around the cell by lipid-transfer proteins. Biochemical approaches have been adapted to measure which lipids are captured by the more than 130 known human lipid-transfer proteins, providing a valuable resource that reveals some principles of how these transporters work.

item.title: Nature: Flexible paths to multicellularity
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00292-7 Close relatives of animals can become multicellular if distinct individuals join together or if dividing cells remain attached. A species has been found to use both mechanisms.

item.title: Nature: Brains of ‘super agers’ are strong producers of new neurons
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00599-5 Older people with exceptional memory have a surprisingly high number of young neurons, study finds.

item.title: Nature: Environmental exposure trains the immune system to dampen allergic responses
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00040-x Clean living conditions that lessen exposure to microorganisms are linked to an increase in allergies. Mouse data reveal how the environment affects allergic immune responses.

item.title: Nature: Scientists face fallout for past associations with Epstein
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00554-4 Jack Horner, who was a consultant for the Jurassic Park films, is among the researchers whose work or careers have been affected because of revelations from newly released documents.

item.title: Nature: Parkinson’s disease affects network of brain regions that controls whole-body action
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00573-1 Precision brain imaging of individuals with Parkinson’s disease reveals that the affected circuit is best characterized as a previously described network of brain regions called the somato-cognitive action network. Abnormally high connectivity in this network is associated with Parkinson’s disease and is normalized by effective pharmacological treatment and various brain-stimulation therapies.

item.title: Nature: The secret of squeaky basketball shoes
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00295-4 When shoes slide across a floor, wave-like deformations of the sole can generate squeaking. The pitch of the squeak depends on the rate at which deformations are generated.

item.title: Nature: The future perfect continuous passive and other transitive disorders of the mind
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00132-8 Grammar is destiny.

item.title: Nature: The first ice-core record of historical atmospheric hydrogen levels
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00578-w An ice-core record of hydrogen reveals that atmospheric levels vary in response to climate change and have increased drastically owing to human activity since the pre-industrial era. The apparent sensitivity of hydrogen cycling to environmental conditions should be considered when projecting the consequences of rising anthropogenic hydrogen emissions in a warming climate.

item.title: Nature: Amplified X-ray laser pulses achieved using mirror set-up
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00580-2 Current X-ray lasers require facilities that are kilometres long. A cavity-based set-up about 66 metres in length has been developed that uses highly reflective mirrors to enable the generation of high-intensity pulses of narrow-band X-ray radiation. This promises to overcome the limitations of current X-ray lasers.

item.title: Nature: What's the best way to change research fields? These three scientists have ideas
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-025-04161-7 Planning to switch fields? Be bold, know your limits and choose your institution wisely, say three UK research leaders.

item.title: Nature: Pop-up journals for policy research: can temporary titles deliver answers?
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00446-7 Journals that focus on specific research questions could help to bridge the science–policy gap, if they can attract researchers.

item.title: Nature: Five ways to spot when a paper is a fraud
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00569-x Science sleuths share their common-sense tips for sniffing out fishy articles.

item.title: Nature: Protein engineering fixes a major crop trade-off
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00293-6 Rational design of a regulatory protein decouples the ability to tolerate cold from the means to acquire phosphorus, effectively enhancing crop yield under cold stress.

item.title: Nature: Light-confining device can control superconductivity — even in the dark
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00296-3 A device based on light-confining materials can modify superconductivity using quantum fluctuations, without the need for external illumination.

item.title: Nature: Sea-urchin spines generate electrical signals in flowing water
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00374-6 The spines of sea urchins can generate a voltage when water moves around them — a phenomenon that could be used to design underwater flow sensors.

item.title: Nature: Lipid nanoparticles engineered to target therapeutic RNA to the pancreas
item.description: Nature, Published online: 25 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00294-5 A two-pronged strategy directs drug-delivering nanoparticles to the pancreas — and shows promise in animal models of serious pancreatic diseases.

item.title: Cell: A regulatory network promotes apoplastic alkalinization to prime plant immunity in tissues distal to site of infection
item.description: Pathogen-exposed plant cells communicate with neighboring cells through apoplastic alkalinization and phytocytokines, which jointly propagate from the pathogen-exposed local tissue to distal tissues, providing a warning system for robust defenses and disease resistance.

item.title: Cell: Editing strigolactone hormone receptor for robust antiviral silencing in rice
item.description: Precise genome editing of the rice strigolactone receptor DWARF14 confers robust, transgene-free antiviral resistance by blocking viral suppression of endogenous RNA silencing, offering a promising strategy for durable disease protection without a yield penalty.

item.title: Cell: Fungal-derived cellobiose metabolic pathway fuels T cells to bypass intratumoral glucose competition
item.description: Equipping T cells with fungal enzymes to utilize cellobiose (a safe and natural disaccharide of glucose obtained from the wood polymer cellulose) enhances their viability and effector function in tumor microenvironments where glucose concentrations are constrained.

item.title: Cell: LUMI-lab: A foundation model-driven autonomous platform enabling discovery of ionizable lipid designs for mRNA delivery
item.description: LUMI lab is a foundation model-driven self-driving platform that autonomously discovers ionizable lipids for mRNA delivery. Iterative active learning uncovered brominated tails as a potent structural motif that enables efficient and safe pulmonary mRNA delivery.

item.title: Nature: Dynamic antigen expression and cytotoxic T cell resistance in HIV reservoir clones
item.description: Nature, Published online: 24 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10298-w Dynamic antigen expression and cytotoxic T cell resistance in HIV reservoir clones

item.title: Nature: The Contributor Role Taxonomy tool must serve to record extent of authorship
item.description: Nature, Published online: 24 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00591-z The Contributor Role Taxonomy tool must serve to record extent of authorship

item.title: Nature: Sewage systems secretly waft pollution into the air
item.description: Nature, Published online: 24 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00514-y Wastewater treatment tanks and other infrastructure emit larger amounts of greenhouse gases than reported.

item.title: Nature: Treasures of scientific history could be hiding in plain sight
item.description: Nature, Published online: 24 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00298-1 A reader calls for museum curators to look for historic scientific apparatus, and a landmark treaty aims to protect the Mediterranean from pollution, in our weekly dip into Nature’s archive.

item.title: Nature: Defunding Chile’s climate research will undermine science and the region
item.description: Nature, Published online: 24 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00592-y Defunding Chile’s climate research will undermine science and the region

item.title: Nature: Account for AI in the environmental footprint of scientific publishing
item.description: Nature, Published online: 24 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00590-0 Account for AI in the environmental footprint of scientific publishing

item.title: Nature: This ant species is composed of only queens — no workers or males
item.description: Nature, Published online: 24 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00517-9 Temnothorax kinomurai queens survive by invading the nests of a related ant species and co-opting its workers.

item.title: Nature: Evidence alone won’t save biodiversity: the golden apple snail reveals an implementation gap
item.description: Nature, Published online: 24 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00593-x Evidence alone won’t save biodiversity: the golden apple snail reveals an implementation gap

item.title: Nature: COVID’s origins: what we do and don’t know
item.description: Nature, Published online: 24 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00530-y Researchers summarize key insights from the world’s first comprehensive investigation into how a pandemic started.

item.title: Nature: Nuclear weapons testing is harmful — there’s no case for a restart
item.description: Nature, Published online: 24 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00561-5 Scientific knowledge about the damaging effects of nuclear-weapons testing helped to end such tests. Those findings haven’t changed.

item.title: Nature: China is waging war on Alzheimer’s. What can its approach teach the rest of the world?
item.description: Nature, Published online: 24 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00564-2 The country is facing a coming wave of dementia for its ageing population, and is investing in research into drugs, diagnostics and even surgery to prepare itself.

item.title: Nature: Scientists must step up to avert a nuclear breakout
item.description: Nature, Published online: 24 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00562-4 The end of the US–Russia treaty to cap the number of nuclear weapons places the world at risk. Here’s what researchers can do.

item.title: Nature: Markovnikov hydroamination of terminal alkenes via phosphine redox catalysis
item.description: Nature, Published online: 23 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10263-7 Markovnikov hydroamination of terminal alkenes via phosphine redox catalysis

item.title: Cell: A GPX1-OSBPL8 axis mediates noncanonical in vivo ferroptosis and cancer growth suppression
item.description: An in vivo , noncanonical ferroptosis pathway, critical for tumor supression, is driven by reactive oxygen species-induced phosphatidic acid peroxidation at the ER under the control of the GPX1-OSBPL8 signaling axis.

item.title: Science: Matching sounds to shapes: Evidence of the bouba-kiki effect in naïve baby chicks
Science: Ribosomal RNA expansion segments mediate the oligomerization of inactive animal ribosomes
Science: Evolution of error correction through a need for speed
Science: Carbonated ultramafic igneous rocks in Jezero crater, Mars
Science: Termination of the integrated stress response
Cell: Brain-wide mapping of oligodendrocyte organization, oligodendrogenesis, and myelin injury
item.description: Generation of brain-wide oligodendrocyte atlases across aging, disease, sex, and strain reveals striking regional differences in myelin abundance, resilience, and vulnerability. Integration with transcriptomic and ultrastructural data identifies factors that may shape this diverse oligodendrocyte patterning.

item.title: Cell: Genomic atlas of Bifidobacterium infantis and B. longum informs infant probiotic design
item.description: A global genomic survey of infant gut bifidobacteria shows that B. infantis remains highly prevalent and diverse in infants from low- and middle-income countries but scarce in Western, industrialized populations and poorly represented in current probiotics. This genomic and culture collection catalogs geo-specific B. infantis strains and provides a blueprint for developing probiotics tailored to local diets and populations to support infant health.

item.title: Cell: Unified modeling of 3D molecular generation via atomic interactions with PocketXMol
item.description: A versatile, atom-level generative AI model enables unified pocket-interacting tasks, from docking to de novo design, and demonstrates robust experimental validation for both small-molecule and peptide therapeutics.

item.title: Cell: Liver exerkine reverses aging- and Alzheimer’s-related memory loss via vasculature
item.description: Liver exercise factor GPLD1 rejuvenates blood-brain barrier integrity and reverses cognitive impairments in aging and Alzheimer’s disease models by targeting GPI-anchored proteins on brain endothelial cells.

item.title: Cell: A circadian rheostat drives proton electrochemical gradients to optimize cell-type-specific growth in Arabidopsis
item.description: The clock component CCA1 functions as a molecular rheostat, fine-tuning cell-type-specific electrochemical gradients to optimize carbon allocation and the timely coordination of shoot and root growth balance.

item.title: Cell: Tuning the sensitivity of mechanosensory receptors through histidine scanning
item.description: Histidine scanning represents a broadly applicable technique for the identification of critical interaction sites within TCRs and other mechanosensory receptors to enhance receptor signaling strength and augment therapeutic efficacy via the catch bond mechanism.

item.title: Cell: Giant DNA viruses encode a hallmark translation initiation complex of eukaryotic life
item.description: Giant DNA viruses encode a cap-binding complex homologous to eIF4F, the defining translation-initiation complex of eukaryotes. The viral cap-binding complex is required for viral protein synthesis and enables an unusual degree of replication plasticity under altered host conditions.

item.title: Cell: Extracellular matrix sensing regulates intratumoral heterogeneity of autophagic flux
item.description: Human pancreatic cancer cells sense specific components of the ECM to fine-tune their autophagy flux levels, conferring the ability to coordinate proliferation, survival, and responsiveness to chemotherapy. Targeting ECM sensing may turn this ability into a therapeutic opportunity.

item.title: Cell: A single-cell time-series atlas of endothelial cell embryonic development
item.description: The STED-EC atlas enables inter-organ and multi-time-point comparisons of gene expression in endothelial cells, revealing substantial transcriptomic variations across endothelial cells from different embryonic organs and facilitating investigation of previously unknown molecular mechanisms that govern organ-specific vascular development.

item.title: Cell: CLIM-TIME identifies metastatic microenvironment modulators for T cell therapy response
item.description: CLIM-TIME provides a high-throughput perturbation-mapping platform that links tumor suppressor gene loss to spatially defined metastatic niches and immune responses, identifying LOXL2 as a key modulator of suppressive metastatic environments. Inhibition of LOXL2 restores T cell infiltration into tumors and improves the efficacy of therapy.

item.title: Cell: Persistent T cell activation and cytotoxicity against glioblastoma following single oncolytic virus treatment in a clinical trial
item.description: Single oncolytic virus treatment in patients with glioblastoma induces deep and persistent T cell activation against tumor cells. Direct and sustained T cell engagement with tumor cells upon treatment correlates with survival outcome.

item.title: Cell: Planetary microbiome structure and generalist-driven gene flow across disparate habitats
item.description: A planetary-scale analysis of over 85,000 metagenomes establishes a framework for exploring the structure and drivers of global microbial habitats, revealing that generalist species bridge ecological boundaries to mediate gene flow across disparate habitats, including the dissemination of antimicrobial resistance.

item.title: Cell: Divergent tumor immunity determined by bacteria-cancer cell engagement
item.description: In a preclinical breast cancer metastasis model, the same bacteria strain, when present intracellularly versus extracellularly, exerts opposing effects on tumor immunity by inducing divergent neutrophil states, highlighting the intricacy in bacterial-host engagement for shaping tumor immunity.

item.title: Cell: Meningeal blood vessel blockage enhances anti-glioblastoma immunity
item.description: Meningeal blood vessel blockage enhances anti-tumor immunity against GBM in preclinical models by expanding dural resident border-associated macrophages, which are equipped with an elevated antigen-presentation function and are poised for effective T cell activation, suggesting a surgical strategy for potentiating GBM immunotherapy.

item.title: Cell: Molecular architecture of human dermal sleeping nociceptors
item.description: Integration of electrophysiology with single-cell transcriptomics defines the molecular signature of human dermal sleeping nociceptors and reveals oncostatin M as a selective modulator of these neurons in humans, providing a therapeutic entry point for neuropathic pain.

item.title: Cell: Hallmarks of cancer—Then and now, and beyond
item.description: Hanahan revisits the evolving framework of cancer hallmarks, synthesizing 25 years of conceptual refinement into a multidimensional view of tumor biology. This review highlights how aberrant capabilities, enabling traits, microenvironmental players, and systemic interactions converge to drive tumorigenesis and proposes that mechanism-guided co-targeting of hallmarks may offer promising therapeutic strategies.

item.title: Cell: Sympathetic-epithelial crosstalk governs tissue-resident memory T cell immunosurveillance in the skin
item.description: Sympathetic nerves regulate skin immunity by engaging keratinocytes to modulate the density of tissue-resident memory T cells. This neuro-epithelial axis can enable the nervous system to dynamically tune local immunosurveillance in barrier tissues against emerging cancers.

item.title: Cell: CRISPR screens in iPSC-derived neurons reveal principles of tau proteostasis
item.description: CRISPR screens in iPSC-derived neurons reveal that the E3 ubiquitin ligase CRL5 SOCS4 ubiquitinates tau, that CUL5 expression is correlated with resilience in human Alzheimer’s disease, and that electron transport chain dysfunction alters tau degradation by the proteasome.

item.title: Cell: An uORF-encoded mobile peptide sparks systemic stomatal immunity
item.description: In Arabidopsis , the uORF-encoded long-distance mobile peptide USIC in pathogen-infected local leaves activates systemic stomatal immunity, leading to stomatal closure in uninfected distal leaves.

item.title: Cell: A GPCR-G protein-β-arrestin megacomplex enabled by a versatile allosteric modulator
item.description: Identification of atazanavir as a pan-positive allosteric modulator for family A GPCRs that stabilizes a unique GPCR-G protein-β-arrestin megacomplex and mediates sustained signaling.

item.title: Cell: MYC binding to nascent RNA suppresses innate immune signaling by R-loop-derived RNA-DNA hybrids
item.description: RNA-binding-mediated multimerization of MYC concentrates RNA-degrading factors around double-stranded RNAs and R-loops. This prevents aberrant RNAs from accumulating and leaking into the cytosol. Through RNA binding, MYC suppresses innate immune signaling and promotes tumor growth.

item.title: Cell: Identification of Or5v1/Olfr110 as an oxylipin receptor and anti-obesity target
item.description: Or5v1/Olfr110, a high-affinity odor receptor, detects an oxylipin signal to boost liver fat burning and glucose control, and a synthetic agonist can amplify this metabolic benefit.

item.title: Cell: Mechanistic insights into fatty acid odor detection mediated by class II olfactory receptors
item.description: Cryo-EM structures reveal how Olfr110, a class II odorant receptor, binds hydrophobic odorants such as unsaturated fatty acid metabolites in a large polar pocket with an unconventional activation mechanism, defining the structural basis of odor recognition and guiding drug targeting.

item.title: Cell: Structural decoding of reversible covalent linkage of odorants in human olfactory receptor OR6A2
item.description: The human olfactory receptor OR6A2, re-engineered to be functional, demonstrates the mechanism by which it detects aldehydes. Using this approach, Wang, Wu, et al. uncovered a broadly conserved activation switch in class II odorant receptors. This work also outlines a practical approach to decode smell, with potential uses in fragrance design and inflammation therapy.

item.title: Cell: Nanoparticles hijack calvarial immune cells for CNS drug delivery and stroke therapy
item.description: Drug-loaded albumin NPs hijack calvarial immune cells to bypass the BBB via skull-meninges microchannels for CNS drug delivery and stroke therapy, establishing skull-based delivery and immune-assisted transport as a clinically translatable strategy for neurological therapeutics.

item.title: Cell: Human genetics guides the discovery of CARD9 inhibitors with anti-inflammatory activity
item.description: A binder-first approach enables the identification of a druggable pocket and compound for the immune protein CARD9 that dampens its inflammatory signaling. This compound reduces cytokine production in immune cells and in a mouse model, demonstrating how therapeutic modulation can mimic effects of a CARD9 variant protective against Crohn’s disease.
